## Pytest

- [Pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/) alternative to [unittest](https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html)
- Extensible (lots of [plugins](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference/plugin_list.html))
- Easy to setup fixtures.
- Easy to parameterise.

### Why?

- Something useful to share.
- I already wrote a [blog post](https://blog.nshephard.dev/posts/pytest-markers/).

## Test Development

- Don't always want to run the whole test suite during development
- Run a single test (`test_slow`)[^emacs]...

```shell
pytest tests/test_something.py::test_slow
```

- Doesn't exclude `test_slow` from the whole suite.
- If `test_slow` takes a long time running whole suite delays feedback.
- **Solution** - Create your own marks to select which tests are run

[^emacs]: Can dispatch individual tests from within Emacs using
[python-pytest](https://github.com/wbolster/emacs-python-pytest) 😉

## Example - Test with marks

```python
import time
import pytest

@pytest.mark.slow
def test_slow() -> None:
    """A dummy test that takes a an hour to run."""
    time.sleep(60*60)
    pass

def test_quick() -> None:
    """A dummy test that takes 2 seconds to run."""
    time.sleep(2)
    pass

def test_very_fast() -> None:
    """A dummy test that takes 1 second to run."""
    time.sleep(1)
    pass
```

## Example - Selectively run tests based on marks

```shell
# Run just `test_slow` that is marked with 'slow'
pytest -v -m "slow"
# Run all other tests that are not marked 'slow'
pytest -v -m "not slow"
```

## Configure via `pyproject.toml`

Configure project to exclude slow tests by default.

```toml
[tool.pytest]
addopts = ["-m", "not slow"]
markers = [
  "slow: marks slow tests (deselect with '-m \"not slow\")",
]
```

## Automatically add markers

- Structured nomenclature of tests to indicates what the tests are doing allows [automation of adding
markers](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/example/markers.html#automatically-adding-markers-based-on-test-names) based
  on test names.

```python
def test_func_function1():
    pass

def test_func_function2():
    pass

def test_exception_keyerror():
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        {"a": 0, "b": 1}["not a key"]

def test_exception_indexerror():
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        [0, 1, 2][3]
```

## Configure via `conftest.py`

:::: {.columns}


::: {.column width="50%"}
```python
import pytest

def pytest_collection_modifyitems(items):
    for item in items:
        if "func" in item.nodeid:
            item.add_marker(
                pytest.mark.func
            )
        elif "exception" in item.nodeid:
            item.add_marker(
                pytest.mark.exception
            )
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}


- `@pytest.mark.func` added if test function includes `func`.
- `@pytest.mark.exception` added if test function includes `exception`.

:::
::::

## Update `pyproject.toml`

```toml
[tool.pytest]
  addopts = ["-m", "not slow"]
  markers = [
    "slow: marks slow tests (deselect with '-m \"not slow\")",
    "func: marks tests of functions (dselect with '-m \"not func\")"
    "exceptions: marks tests of exceptions (dselect with '-m \"not exceptions\")"
  ]
```


## What marks are there?

- Marks may grow over time.
- Use `pytest --marks` to list.


## `@pytest.mark.skip`

- Skip an individual test.
- `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="Don't like this test!")`

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

Whole function

```python
@pytest.mark.skip(
    reason="Don't like this test!"
)
def test_func_function1() -> None:
    pass

```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

Individual paramterised sets

```python
@pytest.mark.parameterise(
    ("string"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            "a",
            id="test1"
        ),
        pytest.param(
            2,
            id="test2",
            marks=pytest.mark.skip(
                reason="Don't like this test!"
            )
        ),
    ]
)
def test_func_function1(string: str) -> None:
    assert isinstance(string, str)

```
:::
::::

## `@pytest.mark.xfail`

- `@pytest.mark.xfail(reason="I know this test fails!")`


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

Whole function

```python
@pytest.mark.xfail(
    reason="I know this test fails!"
)
def test_func_function1() -> None:
    pass

```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

Individual paramterised sets

```python
@pytest.mark.parameterise(
    ("string"),
    [
        pytest.param("a", id="test1"),
        pytest.param(
            2,
            id="test2",
            marks=pytest.mark.xfail(
                reason="I know this test fails!"
            )
        ),
    ]
)
def test_func_function1(string: str) -> None:
    assert isinstance(string, str)

```

:::
::::


## `@pytest.mark.skipif`

- `@pytest.mark.skipif(reason="Don't like this test!")`
- Useful if you now a test always fails on CI in a particular environment or Python version.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

Whole function

```python
import os
import platform

GITHUB_ACTIONS = os.getenv("GITHUB_ACTIONS") == "true"
OSX = platform.system() == "Darwin"

@pytest.mark.skipif(
    GITHUB_ACTIONS and OSX,
    reason="Test fails in CI on OSX!")
def test_func_function1() -> None:
    pass

```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

Individual paramterised sets

```python
import os
import platform

GITHUB_ACTIONS = os.getenv("GITHUB_ACTIONS") == "true"
OSX = platform.system() == "Darwin"

@pytest.mark.parameterise(
    ("string"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            "a",
            id="test1"
        ),
        pytest.param(
            2,
            id="test2",
            marks=pytest.mark.skipif(
                GITHUB_ACTIONS and OSX,
                reason="Test fails in CI on OSX!"
            )
        ),
    ]
)
def test_func_function1(string: str) -> None:
    assert isinstance(string, str)

```

:::
::::

## [Pytest testmon](https://www.testmon.org/)

- Changes typically small
- Only impact subset of tests
- 🪄 [Pytest testmon](https://www.testmon.org/) 🪄

> a pytest plugin which selects and executes only tests you need to run. It does this by collecting dependencies between
>  tests and all executed code (internally using Coverage.py) and comparing the dependencies against changes. testmon
>  updates its database on each test execution, so it works independently of version control.

```toml
[dependency-groups]
tests = [
  ...
  "pytest-testmon"
  ...
]
```

## As a `pre-commit` hook

- On commits `pytest --testmon` run only on affected changes.

```yaml
   - repo: local
     hooks:
       - id: pytest
         name: Pytest (testmon)
         entry: pytest --testmon
         language: system
         files: \.py$
```

## Summary

- Lots of different strategies for managing test suite!
- Structured nomenclature of tests can be very useful.
- Use any or many of these to speed up the feedback loop.
